title: North East Derbyshire District Council: using Copilot to support better decisions and organisational change
summary: North East Derbyshire District Council uses Microsoft Copilot for drafting, summaries and analysis and expects it to cut repetitive work; it reports no measured saving.
account: North East Derbyshire District Council introduced Copilot alongside governance, data and skills programs to improve decisions and service design. The council describes more evidence-seeking staff discussions and changes in decision practice. It does not isolate the contribution of Copilot from the wider program. The council still expects reductions in repetitive work and better outcomes for residents.
purpose: Reduce routine drafting, reporting, and information-handling work so that staff have more time for analysis and service improvement.

ratings.reason: The council expects Copilot to reduce repetitive reporting and information-handling work. No realized AI-produced efficiency or decision-quality improvement is established.
Staff are intended to spend less time on repetitive tasks and more time on analysis. The source does not establish that AI produced the reported confidence or critical-questioning gains.

ai_role.statement: The source identifies Copilot drafting, summarization, and analysis uses. Their operational benefits remain expected. It does not establish that AI produced the staff-confidence or evidence-seeking changes observed in the wider training and governance program.
